summary: Chevening is the UK Government's scholarship for future leaders. It pays for a one-year master's at a UK university: full tuition, a monthly stipend, return flights and visa costs. Winners are people with at least two years of real work experience who can show clear leadership, strong networks and a concrete plan to make change at home.
lookfor: Leadership and influence: times you took the lead, persuaded others and got a clear result
Networking: strong working relationships you built and what they achieved
Course choice: how your three UK courses (and specific modules) connect to your background and goals
Career plan: short, medium and long-term goals that are clear and measurable
Commitment to return home for at least two years and use what you learn there
Original writing in your own words (AI-generated or copied essays are disqualified)
cycle: The 2027/28 round closed on 6 October 2026 (11:00 UTC). Shortlists come mid-February 2027, interviews run March–April 2027, results from mid-June 2027, and the unconditional university offer is due 8 July 2027. The next round usually opens in early August 2027 and closes in early October 2027 — use this guide to prepare for it.

eligibility.q: Are you a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country and will you apply from that country?
eligibility.no: You cannot apply through another country's programme. Look at the Commonwealth Master's Scholarship or university-funded awards instead.

eligibility.q: Did you finish your undergraduate degree at least two years before the application deadline, and does it qualify you for a UK master's?
eligibility.no: Wait until you meet the two-year rule and build work experience meanwhile. Check each course's entry requirements for your degree class.

eligibility.q: Do you have at least 2,800 hours of work experience gained after your degree?
eligibility.no: Full-time, part-time, voluntary work and internships all count. Keep working and apply in the round where you pass 2,800 hours. The online form calculates it and rejects you automatically if you fall short.

eligibility.q: Will you return to your home country for at least two years after your course?
eligibility.no: Chevening is not for you. Consider awards without a return condition, such as university scholarships.

eligibility.q: Are you free of British citizenship, recent UK government / British Council employment (including immediate family), and previous UK-government-funded study in the UK?
eligibility.no: You are not eligible. Former Chevening Fellows must wait five years. Consider Commonwealth (if you have never held one) or university awards.

eligibility.q: Can you get an unconditional offer from at least one of three different eligible UK master's courses by early July?
eligibility.no: Start university applications early and meet each course's English requirement; without an unconditional offer the award cannot go ahead.

steps.title: Check you are eligible before you invest time
steps.why: Most rejected forms fail on eligibility, not quality. The system checks you at the start and gives only four retries.
do: Open the official eligibility guidance and read every line.
Write down the date your degree was completed (final results date, not convocation) and confirm it is at least two years before an early-October deadline.
List every job, volunteer role and internship since your degree with start date, end date and hours per week.
Multiply weeks × hours per week for each role and add them up. You need 2,800 or more.
Check you have no UK government, British Council or partner-university employment in the last two years (and no immediate family who do).
tips: Your NYSC year comes after your degree and is full-time work, so it usually counts — enter the real hours.
Volunteering and unpaid internships count too; include them if your hours are short.
avoid: Inflating hours (e.g. 80 hours a week) — selectors notice unrealistic numbers.
Listing the same job twice to reach the total.
check: I can say yes to every eligibility question with evidence.
My calculated hours are 2,800 or more.

steps.title: Learn what selectors score
steps.why: Chevening scores four areas: leadership, networking, course choice and career plan. Every essay and interview answer must give evidence for one of them.
do: Open the application criteria page and copy the four areas into a notebook.
Under each area, write three real stories from your work or community life.
For each story note: the situation, what you did, who you influenced, and the measurable result.
Read the common errors page and tick off each mistake you will avoid.
tips: Stories with numbers (people reached, money saved, policy changed) beat general claims.
avoid: Treating it as an academic scholarship; grades matter far less than leadership evidence.
check: I have at least two strong stories for each of the four areas.

steps.title: Build your personal timeline
steps.why: The form is open for only about nine weeks. People who start writing when it opens rush and submit weak essays.
do: Open the application timeline page and note the stages.
Put the expected opening (early August) and closing (early October) dates in your calendar, then set reminders 60, 30 and 7 days before closing.
Block two evenings a week from June for essay drafting.
Subscribe for Chevening updates so you get the exact dates when announced.
tips: Aim to submit at least a week early — the portal gets slow near the deadline.
avoid: Waiting for the form to open before writing anything.
check: My calendar has the key dates and writing blocks.

steps.title: Choose your three UK courses
steps.why: You must pick three different eligible one-year master's courses. A weak or random choice undermines your 'why UK' essay.
do: Open the Chevening course finder and search your field.
Shortlist six courses, then read each course page: modules, entry requirements, English test score, application deadline and fee.
Pick three different courses (not the same course three times) that all serve one career goal.
For each, note two or three named modules and how each builds a skill you need.
Check if any are Chevening partner awards for your country — they can improve your chances.
tips: Choose courses that sit within UK priority areas and clearly link to a problem at home.
Note which universities charge application fees and which waive them.
avoid: Choosing three courses at the same university that are basically identical.
Picking only top-ranked courses where your degree class may not get an unconditional offer.
check: I have three different eligible courses and can explain each in two sentences.

steps.title: Get your documents ready early
steps.why: You need a passport and your degree certificate by interview time, and universities need transcripts and English results to give an unconditional offer.
do: Passport: check it is valid until at least late 2028. If not, apply for renewal now (Nigeria: NIS online portal; allow several weeks).
Degree certificate: if you have not collected it, contact your university's Exams and Records / Academic Office now. Chevening wants the official certificate, not a transcript.
Transcripts: request official transcripts for your universities through your university's transcript portal or registry. Budget the naira fee and courier cost; it can take 2–8 weeks.
English test: check each course's requirement. Many UK universities accept a medium-of-instruction letter from Nigerian universities; otherwise book IELTS early.
Save scans as clear PDFs named e.g. 'Surname_Passport.pdf'.
tips: Chevening itself does not set an English test — your universities do.
Ask your university for an English-proficiency (medium of instruction) letter at the same time as transcripts.
avoid: Leaving the degree certificate until you are shortlisted — collection can take months.
check: I have, or have requested, passport, degree certificate, transcripts and English evidence.

steps.title: Write the leadership and influencing essay
steps.why: Leadership is the first thing Chevening looks for. Selectors want proof that you have led and influenced others to a clear result.
do: Pick your strongest one or two leadership stories from your notes.
Structure each: situation (2 lines), your action and how you persuaded people (most of the words), result with numbers, what you learned.
Show influence: who disagreed, how you won them over.
Cut adjectives; keep verbs and facts.
Read it aloud and trim to the limit.
tips: Leadership need not be a title — leading a change in your team or community counts.
Link the lesson to the leader you plan to become.
avoid: Listing many roles with no depth.
Using AI to write it — Chevening screens for AI text and disqualifies it.
check: A stranger can say exactly what I did and what changed because of me.

steps.prompt: Show how you have taken the lead and influenced others, with clear results (paraphrased).
steps.limit: Check the form — recent rounds allowed up to about 500 words.

steps.title: Write the networking essay
steps.why: Chevening is a lifelong network. They want people who build working relationships that lead to measurable outcomes.
do: Pick one or two examples where a relationship you built produced a result (a partnership, funding, a joint project).
Explain how you built it: who, why, how you kept it going.
State the outcome with numbers.
End with how you will use and grow the Chevening and UK network for your goals.
tips: Name types of people (e.g. state ministry officials, NGO leads), not just 'stakeholders'.
avoid: Talking about networking as collecting LinkedIn contacts.
check: My essay shows a relationship that produced a concrete result.
steps.prompt: Explain how you build strong working relationships and how collaboration led to measurable outcomes (paraphrased).
steps.limit: Check the form — recent rounds allowed up to about 500 words.

steps.title: Write the 'why these UK courses' essay
steps.why: You must show your three courses connect to your background and goals, and why the UK is the right place.
do: Open your notes on the three courses.
Start with the problem or goal at home the courses help you solve.
For each course, name specific modules and the skill each gives you.
Say why studying in the UK (not at home) matters: expertise, methods, networks.
Link back to your career plan.
tips: Use real module names; generic praise for 'world-class universities' scores poorly.
avoid: Writing only about one course and ignoring the other two.
check: Each course is mentioned with at least one specific module.
steps.prompt: Explain your choice of three UK courses, how they connect to your background and career, and how specific modules will equip you (paraphrased).
steps.limit: Check the form — recent rounds allowed up to about 500 words.

steps.title: Write the career plan essay
steps.why: Selectors want a realistic short, medium and long-term plan with measurable goals, rooted in your home country.
do: Write your long-term goal (10+ years) in one sentence.
Work backwards: what job/role in the first 1–2 years after return, and what by year 5?
Give each stage a measurable target (e.g. 'train 200 extension officers').
Name real organisations you will work with or join.
Show how the UK master's and the Chevening network make each step possible.
tips: Be ambitious but believable — selectors check that the steps follow logically.
avoid: Plans that need you to stay abroad; you must return for two years.
check: My plan has three stages, each with a measurable target.
steps.prompt: Set out a short, medium and long-term career plan with clear, measurable goals (paraphrased).
steps.limit: Check the form — recent rounds allowed up to about 500 words.

steps.title: Choose and brief two referees
steps.why: You give referee names in the form; the letters are needed later if you are shortlisted. Missing them before the interview disqualifies you.
do: Choose two people who know you well professionally or academically (two work, two academic, or one of each). Not friends or relatives.
Ask them now and confirm their correct job titles and emails.
Send each a one-page brief: your goals, your three courses, and two stories they can confirm.
Tell them the letter must be in English and should cover leadership, networking, personal qualities and your ability to complete a UK master's.
Agree that, if shortlisted, they will send a signed letter within a week of your request.
tips: A line manager who saw your leadership is often stronger than a famous professor who barely knows you.
avoid: Choosing referees who are hard to reach in February–March.
check: Both referees have agreed and have my brief.

steps.title: Register and complete the online form
steps.why: The form has seven sections and logs you out after 15 minutes of inactivity. Careless errors make you ineligible.
do: When the round opens, go to chevening.org/apply and register with your email and phone number.
Pass the eligibility check and save your unique access code (take a photo of it).
Fill in Personal details (name as in passport, interview location), Immigration details, Education, Work history (up to 15 entries), three courses, two referees and Equal opportunities.
Paste your final essays from a document into the four essay boxes.
Click save after every section.
tips: Draft essays offline first, then paste — you won't lose work if logged out.
avoid: Entering hours that do not match your dates.

steps.title: Proofread and submit early
do: Read every answer aloud once more and check names, dates and course titles.
Ask one trusted person to read the essays for clarity (not to rewrite them).
Submit at least three days before the 11:00 UTC deadline (12:00 noon in Nigeria).
Keep the confirmation email and screenshot the submitted status.
tips: Note the 11:00 UTC deadline is in the morning.
avoid: Submitting in the last hour when the site is busy.

steps.title: Apply to your three universities and chase an unconditional offer
steps.why: You need at least one unconditional offer by early July or you lose the award, even if you win.
do: Apply to all three courses soon after submitting (many open in October).
Upload transcripts, English evidence, personal statement and references each university asks for.
Pay or request waivers for application fees.
Meet any conditions (final certificate, English score) quickly.
Track offers in a table.
tips: Some courses fill early — apply in October or November.
avoid: Waiting for Chevening results before applying to universities.

steps.title: If shortlisted: upload documents and prepare for interview
steps.why: The interview is a competency-based panel with British High Commission staff. Documents are due seven working days before it.
do: Watch your email from mid-February; book an interview slot immediately.
Upload photo ID, your undergraduate certificate and both reference letters at least seven working days before the interview.
Re-read your essays: the panel questions come from them.
Practise answers on leadership, networking, course choice, career plan and what you will give back to the Chevening network.
Do two mock interviews with a past scholar or colleague. Bring your passport or national ID on the day.
tips: Use the STAR shape (situation, task, action, result) for every example.
Know where your university applications stand — they ask.
avoid: Memorised speeches; answer the question asked.
check: Documents uploaded at least seven working days early.
I have practised aloud at least twice.

links.t: Watch: Chevening interview: How to prepare for your interview in 2025 (Chevening FCDO)

steps.title: Results, conditional award and pre-departure
steps.why: Results come from mid-June. Winning is conditional on an unconditional offer and visa.
do: Check email from mid-June for your result.
Upload your unconditional offer by the July deadline (8 July 2027 for this round).
Follow Chevening's instructions on medical checks, visa and flights.
If unsuccessful, ask yourself which criterion was weakest and strengthen it for next August.
tips: Many winners applied two or three times — reapplying is normal.
check: I know my next action whatever the result.

faq.q: Do I need IELTS for Chevening?
faq.a: Chevening does not set its own English test. Your universities do, and you need their unconditional offer.

faq.q: Does NYSC count as work experience?
faq.a: It is full-time work after your degree, so it usually counts. Enter the real weeks and hours.

faq.q: Do I need a university offer before I apply?
faq.a: No. You need one unconditional offer by the July deadline after selection.

faq.q: Can I use AI to help with essays?
faq.a: No. Chevening prohibits AI-generated answers and screens for them.

faq.q: I missed the October 2026 deadline. What now?
faq.a: The next round usually opens in early August 2027. Use the months until then to build evidence and draft essays.
